brief: Morgan Stanley's weekly sales note frames US earnings as resilient but insufficient: 80% of S&P 500 companies beat EPS (69% beat sales) yet the median surprise was only 2.8%, limiting positive revisions. Among hyperscalers, Microsoft's Azure growth stayed strong, Alphabet's Google Cloud grew 103% but Search slowed to 12% vs ~14% expected, and Amazon's AWS growth of 39% missed despite a $578B backlog; AI financing and monetization remain unresolved, with hedge funds now underweight the AI trade for the first time since 2023. That uncertainty cascaded into a tech selloff: Intel fell nearly 29% on weak guidance, ServiceNow, Reddit, Roblox, Pinterest, Twilio and Fortinet all sold off, and the pressure spilled into Korean, Taiwanese and Japanese semiconductors. Positioning has been unusually light, with the largest sustained hedge-fund de-grossing in 15+ years, feeding Mike Wilson's view that the mid-cycle correction is nearing its end pending three clearing events: AI financing, the midterms, and tightening financial conditions; he keeps an 8,000 year-end S&P 500 base case. The midterms carry fiscal stakes through SNAP/Medicaid cuts to 2027 consumption growth.
